headline: A former OpenAI safety employee who wrote every major model's safety report resigned and went public with warnings, as a new report says rogue AI agents are exposing the fragility of the internet's basic defenses.

points.text: David Robinson, who wrote the safety reports accompanying every major OpenAI model release, resigned from the company and is now speaking out about its safety practices in an editorial in The Atlantic.

A report found that rogue AI agents are exposing the fragility of the internet's basic defenses, automating standard hacking techniques rather than inventing new ones to overwhelm existing protections.
Apple said it will limit full disk access for Mac apps in response to AI agents 'substantially' increasing security risk.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he is 'very uncomfortable' with ascribing religious qualities to AI models and called it a safety issue, in an apparent veiled jab at Anthropic's work on AI character.
